title: Ginsenoside compound K exerts anti-inflammatory effects through transcriptional activation and transcriptional inhibition of glucocorticoid receptor in rheumatoid arthritis fibroblast-like synoviocytes.
authors: Yang, Mei; Mao, Lijuan; Yang, Xingyue; Xu, Xiujin; Tang, Caihong; Wei, Wei; Chen, Jingyu
one_liner_zh: 该文研究人参皂苷GCK与糖皮质激素受体GR的结合及抗炎机制，涉及分子对接但核心是GR-配体而非TF-DNA互作，且无AI/物理模拟方法，仅边缘相关。
abstract: Ginsenoside compound K (GCK) has anti-inflammatory and immunoregulatory effects, and glucocorticoid receptor (GR) has been considered as its potential target. But the mechanism by which GCK exerts its anti-inflammatory effects after GR activation remains unclear. In this study, molecular docking, isothermal titration calorimetry, siRNA of GR and GRA458T mutation were used to confirm the anti-inflammatory mechanism of GCK targeting GR in fibroblast-like synoviocytes (FLS). The results showed that the key binding sites of GR and GCK were identified as ASN564, MET560 and ASN638, with binding levels at the mum level. In addition, the inhibitory effect of GCK on the proliferation of FLS and the secretion of inflammatory cytokines (IL-6, IL-8, and IL-1beta) were mediated by transcriptional activation of GR, but on the migration, invasion, and TNF-alpha secretion of FLS were mediated by transcriptional inhibition of GR. These actions exert anti-inflammatory effects through indirect and direct inhibition of NF-kappaB transcriptional activity, respectively. In conclusion, this study elucidates that GCK can directly bind to and activate GR. Furthermore, after activation, GR mediates the anti-inflammatory effects of GCK through two mechanisms: transcriptional activation and transcriptional inhibition.
abstract_zh: 人参皂苷化合物K（GCK）具有抗炎和免疫调节作用，且糖皮质激素受体（GR）被认为是其潜在靶点。然而，GCK在激活GR后发挥抗炎作用的机制尚不清楚。本研究采用分子对接、等温滴定量热法、GR的siRNA及GRA458T突变，以确认GCK在成纤维样滑膜细胞（FLS）中靶向GR的抗炎机制。结果表明，GR与GCK的关键结合位点被确定为ASN564、MET560和ASN638，结合水平处于微摩尔级。此外，GCK对FLS增殖及炎症细胞因子（IL-6、IL-8和IL-1β）分泌的抑制作用由GR的转录激活介导，而其对FLS迁移、侵袭及TNF-α分泌的作用则由GR的转录抑制介导。这些作用分别通过间接和直接抑制NF-κB转录活性发挥抗炎效应。总之，本研究阐明GCK可直接结合并激活GR。进一步地，在激活后，GR通过两种机制介导GCK的抗炎作用：转录激活和转录抑制。
